newsitem.title: FRANCE: Carmakers quibble over the right lira rate.
newsitem.headline: Carmakers quibble over the right lira rate.

text.p: French carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen chairman Jacques Calvet said on Tuesday he considered that the Italian lira was still undervalued despite its recent rise, but Fiat's deputy chairman said the Italian currency was now overvalued.
Calvet told a news conference he believed a proper exchange rate would be 3.80 francs to 1,000 lire, compared with around 3.38/3.39 francs per 1,000 lire at present.
On Tuesday at 1135 GMT, the franc was worth 294.70 lire while the mark was trading at 997.65 lire.
Fiat Auto managing director Roberto Testore told reporters the lira appeared overvalued and he estimated the right level at 1,040 lire to the German mark.
France has blamed the low value of the lira for hurting French industry competitiveness.
On Tuesday, President Jacques Chirac said the devaluation of the lira, pound sterling and spanish peseta had hurt the textile industry more than competition from Asian markets.
Calvet has said the lira's weakness has hurt French industry, and the car industry in particular, by creating a competitive disadvantage and reducing earnings translated from lire into francs.
He said the Bank of France believed that countries with weak currencies would be penalised in the long run.
"The difference between us and the Bank of France is that we have to live through these periods which for the central bank are spaces in charts," Calvet said.
